summary: GCP -> AWS federated identity bridge failing: sts:AssumeRole denied for private-deploy debug sessions
description:
Issue summary: Engineers cannot assume AWS cross-account roles via GCP Workload Identity federation when initiating private-deploy debugging sessions for customer VPCs. Impact: Blocked debugging access to multiple private-deploy customers in us-west region; delays incident response and capacity debugging. Observed error: 'An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity operation: The provided web identity token is invalid or expired' followed by 'sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity denied by role trust/conditions'.

Environment: Production (private-deploy), us-west cluster connecting to customer-account-aws (account ID masked). Affected teams: SRE, Private Deploy ops, Oncall.

Steps to reproduce:
1. From a GKE bastion (prod-us-west-connect) run: gcloud auth print-identity-token --audiences="sts.amazonaws.com" --include-email
2. Export token and run aws sts assume-role-with-web-identity --role-arn arn:aws:iam::XXXXXXXXXXXX:role/redwood-cross-account-debug --role-session-name=debug-session --web-identity-token file://idtoken.txt
3. Observe AccessDenied / invalid token message.

Immediate business impact: Multiple customer incident debug windows are delayed; rollbacks and log pulls blocked for private deployments. This has triggered manual escalation to SRE.

Requested outcome: Identify root cause (policy/trust/audience mismatch or org SCP block), apply temporary remediation to restore assume-role flows for oncall, and implement a durable fix and tests in CI.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:18 - Priya Nair: Filed after reproducing failure during oncall rotation. Captured token and initial logs attached to PR above.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Riley Patel: I can reproduce from prod bastion. Will collect AWS STS logs and GCP token payload. Prioritizing for P1.

2026-03-13 14:22 - Diego Ramos (security): Early hypothesis: org-level SCP or Permission Boundary may be preventing AssumeRole for roles with external provider conditions. Need AWS Org admin confirmation.

2026-03-14 08:30 - Riley Patel: Temporary workaround applied: created short-lived helper role in customer debug account with explicit trust to our verified OIDC provider and mapped audience. Oncall can now assume via the helper role. Will track rollback window.
2026-03-14 12:10 - Priya Nair: Please add to Workload Identity runbook and create a staging test that runs assume-role-with-web-identity daily.
investigation_notes: Checked AWS CloudTrail for sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity entries: found 403 AccessDenied with errorCode 'AccessDenied', principal: arn:aws:sts::XXXXXXXX:assumed-role/IDP, requestParameters show provider 'accounts.google.com' in token audience mismatch.

Decoded GCP identity token: aud claim set to 'https://sts.googleapis.com' for current helper flow; expected 'sts.amazonaws.com' for cross-account assume-role-with-web-identity. Token was minted by gcloud with default audience in our cluster image; mismatch introduced after gcloud SDK upgrade in prod image on 2026-02-28.

Checked AWS trust policy on role 'redwood-cross-account-debug': Condition has StringLike: 'sts:Audience': 'sts.amazonaws.com' and a 'StringEquals' on 'token.actions/claim' expecting 'projects/-/locations/-/workloadIdentityPools/redwood-pool/subject'. The gcloud-minted token had an OIDC issuer claim that did not match due to new audience formatting.

Reviewed org SCPs: no explicit deny for sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, but there is an account-level permission boundary restricting 'sts:AssumeRole' to roles with tag 'trusted-by:redwood'. The updated helper roles lacked that tag, so even with correct audience they would be denied in some customer accounts.
Runbook checks: No automated CI test currently asserts aud claim mapping between GCP token and AWS trust policy. No synthetic test runs in staging for cross-cloud assume flows.

Commands run: gcloud auth print-identity-token --audiences=\"sts.amazonaws.com\" --include-email > idtoken.txt; aws sts assume-role-with-web-identity --debug --role-arn ... produced header: 'X-Amz-Sts-Error: AccessDenied' and response showing 'TokenWithInvalidAudience'.
resolution: Workaround (applied 2026-03-14 08:30): Provisioned a temporary helper role in customer debug accounts with explicit trust to the current GCP OIDC token format and added tag 'trusted-by:redwood' to satisfy permission boundary. Oncall validated assume-role flow for three impacted customers.

Root cause: Two changes converged: (1) gcloud SDK update changed default audience formatting for identity tokens in our prod bastion image; (2) some customer accounts enforce permission boundaries that require specific role tags. The combination caused AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity to be denied.

Permanent remediation plan:
- Update prod bastion image to pin gcloud SDK to confirmed version and add explicit --audiences='sts.amazonaws.com' invocation in our helper scripts (target: 2026-03-18).
- Update infra templates to ensure cross-account roles include tag 'trusted-by:redwood' and add an automated policy test during account bootstrap (target: 2026-03-25).
- Add synthetic e2e check in CI that mints a token and runs assume-role-with-web-identity against a staging cross-account role daily (target: 2026-03-20).
- Coordinate with Security and Account Owners to validate permission boundaries and publish guidance for private-deploy customers (target: 2026-03-22).
Follow-ups: Create a short postmortem note in Confluence and add a monitoring alert for repeated 'TokenWithInvalidAudience' errors in CloudTrail and GCP IAM logs.
